newsitem.title: USA: Aetna to pay $300 million for stake in Brazil venture.
newsitem.headline: Aetna to pay $300 million for stake in Brazil venture.

text.p: Aetna Inc. said Monday it has an agreement in principle to invest at least $300 million for a 49 percent stake in a joint venture with Sul America Seguros, Brazil's largest insurance company.
The Sao Paulo-based venture, to be called Sul America Aetna, would provide health and life insurance as well as pension plans in Brazil.
Aetna's initial investment would be approximately $300 million, with up to an additional $90 million over time based on future performance of the venture, the company said.

"This alliance with Brazil's leading health and life insurer would give both Aetna and Sul America a strong presence in an extremely attractive market with a growing demand for private insurance and a stabilising economy," said Richard L. Huber, vice chairman of Aetna.
"It would also position Aetna as the leading health insurer in both Brazil and Mexico, the largest countries in Latin America with two of the fastest-growing economies," he said.

Under the deal, Sul America Seguros would contribute its existing life and health insurance businesses to the joint venture, while Aetna would provide product and marketing expertise, particularly in the fields of health care, pensions and life insurance.
The transaction is expected to be in place by second quarter of this year, the company said.
Aetna's stock was up 75 cents at $79.75 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
